screening_results.reason: This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study comparing cortical grey matter measures between amphetamine-type stimulant users and drug-naïve controls. The paper reports whole-brain vertex-wise analyses of cortical thickness and cortical volume using Freesurfer (QDEC) with cluster-based correction, and presents between-group contrasts (experienced vs. controls; low-exposure vs. controls; etc.), satisfying whole-brain GM comparison requirements. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (Freesurfer v5.0, FSL FIRST) are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 are met. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analysis or non-empirical paper) apply.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using VBM (modulated GM segments) to compare alcohol-dependent patients (n=19) with healthy controls (n=20). It performs voxel-wise analyses (one-sample and between-group two-sample t-tests) of an asymmetry index derived from whole-brain GM maps (processed with SPM8/VBM8 and DARTEL) and reports cluster results with peak MNI coordinates and cluster sizes. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (daily intake, dependence duration, abstinence), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Results are not limited to ROI-only analyses and voxelwise between-group contrasts are provided (within a right-hemispheric gray matter mask) with appropriate multiple-comparison correction. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for empirical whole-brain voxelwise GM analyses comparing substance users (alcohol) and controls and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing cocaine-use disorder (CUD) participants to healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL-VBM, permutation-based ‘randomise’) and reports between-group results (tables/figures) including coordinates and cluster information. Participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets I2 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I3 (reports whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users vs controls), I4 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures/supplement), and I5 (participant and MRI/method details provided). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (PNC sample) comparing adolescent/young adult cannabis users (occasional and frequent) to non-users, reporting measures of gray matter volume and gray matter density. The paper reports whole-brain analyses (global, lobar, and regional/parcelwise contrasts), provides regional maps and analytic code, and applies voxelwise-style testing across the brain (396 comparisons) with FDR correction. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (ANTs, FreeSurfer, R/mgcv) are reported. Thus it satisfies I2, I3, I4, and I5. It is not an ROI-only study nor a non-empirical paper, and the provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language longitudinal structural MRI study comparing gray matter volumes between heavy-drinking adolescents and non-drinking controls (meets I2). The analysis used atlas-based parcellation covering the neocortex and lobar regions and reports whole-brain regional between-group trajectory contrasts (meets I3). Participant demographics (age/sex), substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SRI24 atlas, FSL FAST, lme4 in R) are reported (meets I5). Although results are reported as atlas-based regional volumes rather than voxelwise coordinate tables, inclusion criteria allow whole-brain contrasts and do not require coordinate reporting (I4 not applicable). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not an ROI-only paper restricted to small, local ROIs (it covers the whole neocortex), and it is an empirical human MRI study (E5 and E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis, with moderate-to-high confidence.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing abstinent alcoholics and controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics, drinking history, MRI field strength (3T), and processing/statistics (meets I5). However, the paper uses semi-automated/manual regional segmentation and reports volumes for a predefined ‘reward network’ and individual ROIs rather than presenting any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or whole-brain VBM-style results. Therefore it does not meet I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast) and does not provide qualifying voxelwise whole-brain results as per I4. As a result, it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing grey matter volumes between heavy alcohol-using adolescents/young adults and matched light-drinking controls. The paper reports a whole-brain VBM between-group contrast (stating no significant clusters on whole-brain analysis) and ROI-corrected voxelwise results with coordinates/figures for regions showing reduced GM in users. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (AUDIT-C history), MRI field strength (3 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8/SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing treatment-seeking cocaine users (iCUD) with healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (Group main effects and planned whole-brain comparisons) with coordinate tables/figures (Table 2, Figure 1), satisfying voxelwise reporting. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion requirements for whole-brain GM volume studies of a substance user group (stimulants) vs controls. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (two-sample t-tests) with voxelwise results (peaks plotted in MNI space, clusters reported and discussed) rather than ROI-only analyses. MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5/SPM5), and participant demographics (age, sex distribution) and substance-use characteristics are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing heavy cannabis users (n=20 persistent CB) to matched healthy controls (n=22) with voxelwise VBM analyses. The paper reports whole-brain analyses (exploratory whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters and coordinates, e.g., superior temporal gyrus and medial temporal clusters) and ROI analyses, with voxelwise results presented and described. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM VBM8, DARTEL), and substance use measures (CUDIT, grams/week). Full introduction, methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I2: it reports cortical thickness using surface-based morphometry rather than grey matter volume/density/concentration measures required by the review. It does meet I3 (reports whole-brain vertex-wise between-group contrasts corrected for multiple comparisons), I4 (whole-brain voxel/vertex-wise results are presented in figures/tables and supplementary material), and I5 (reports participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are met. Full text is complete and sufficient for this determination.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry to compare current-smokers (n=315) with never-smokers (n=659). The paper reports whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts with FWE-corrected results and provides voxel coordinates (Table 2) and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), smoking characteristics (pack-years, cigarettes/day, age at onset), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are all reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for nicotine studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study is empirical, in English, and uses whole-brain voxelwise MRI analyses, but it does NOT report whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. Instead it reports continuous associations between alcohol/cannabis use (AUDIT score, TLFB days) and GM/WM measures in pooled cross-sectional samples. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria: I2 (requires between-group comparisons of users vs controls) and I3 (requires at least one whole-brain between-group contrast). It does satisfy I4 (voxelwise/whole-brain results reported in figures/tables) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance measures, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing cocaine-dependent patients (stimulant class) to matched healthy controls. The full text includes introduction, methods, participant details (age, sex, substance-use characteristics), MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and statistical software (VBM toolbox, SPM5), and reports whole-brain between-group voxel-wise contrasts with coordinates and cluster statistics (reduced GM in left striatum and right supramarginal gyrus). These satisfy the review objective and inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing cocaine-dependent individuals (stimulant users) to non-drug-using controls. The full text includes introduction, methods (3T scanner, SPM8/VBM8 preprocessing), participant demographics (age, all male), substance-use characteristics, and voxel-wise GM between-group contrasts and group x impulsivity interactions reported at whole-brain FWE-corrected thresholds. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM differences), I3 (whole-brain between-group contrasts), I4 (voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures), and I5 (reports age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs controls and reports total gray- and white-matter volumes and ICV, but it does not present any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts, coordinate tables, or regional voxelwise GM results (only global/volume ratios). Therefore it meets inclusion criterion I2 (empirical MRI assessing GM volume differences) but does NOT meet I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported) nor I4 (no voxelwise coordinate/figure results provided). Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the paper provides no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results (only global/region-aggregate volumes). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing methamphetamine-exposed monkeys (N=7) to saline controls (N=7) with voxel-wise morphometry and behavioral/PET correlations. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing substance-exposed vs controls), I4 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), I5 (participant age/sex, dosing, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (does NOT report a whole-brain between-group contrast corrected across the entire brain; analyses were confined to a predefined set of ROIs and corrected for the search volume within those ROIs rather than whole-brain inference). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (analyses are effectively ROI-restricted with no qualifying whole-brain results). Additionally, the study uses non-human (vervet monkey) subjects which makes it incompatible with the human-focused meta-analysis scope, reinforcing exclusion. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (VBM) comparing heroin abusers to healthy controls with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and corrected cluster results. The paper reports between-group GM volume differences (heroin vs controls), uses whole-brain voxelwise two-way ANOVA with multiple-comparison correction, and provides neuroimaging methods (1.5T scanner, SPM8/DARTEL preprocessing, FSL for DTI), participant demographics/substance-use criteria, and imaging results (clusters, correlations, connectivity). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing treatment-naive alcohol-dependent individuals (n=24) to controls (n=17). It reports whole-brain measures (total cortical gray matter differences) and regional cortical gray matter volume differences (prefrontal and parietal regions) between groups, acquired on a 1.5T scanner with detailed preprocessing and statistical methods described. Participant demographics (male, ages described), substance use characteristics (lifetime duration, consumption), MRI field strength, and software/statistics (SAS PROC GLM) are reported. The study is not ROI-only (it includes whole-brain total cortical gray matter contrasts and regional analyses mapped in the Talairach system), so it meets the review’s requirements for whole-brain between-group GM comparisons and provides usable regional results relevant to the meta-analysis objective. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI (VBM) study of binge-drinking (alcohol) subjects vs healthy volunteers that reports whole-brain voxel-wise analyses. The Methods describe T1 acquisition at 3T, preprocessing (SPM8, DARTEL), and whole-brain voxel-wise group comparisons with cluster-level correction; Results report voxel-wise correlations and a between-group comparison (stated as non-significant in highlighted regions). Participant demographics, substance-use measures (AUDIT), MRI field strength, and processing software are provided. Thus it addresses the meta-analysis objective (alcohol users) and satisfies inclusion criteria for empirical GM volume comparisons with whole-brain voxel-wise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter volume between adolescent cannabis users and matched controls. The full text provides introduction, detailed methods (participants, 3T MRI acquisition, SPM8 VBM/DARTEL preprocessing, AFNI statistical analyses), results of whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (with cluster-corrected significance, figures and tables), and discussion. Substance use characteristics, participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not a review). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing substance user groups (cannabis-dependent and nicotine-dependent) to healthy controls. It directly addresses the review objective for cannabis and nicotine classes. The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain between-group contrasts with cluster-level FWE correction and presents regional cluster results; participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

While this is an empirical English-language VBM study of methamphetamine users and controls that reports whole-brain voxelwise results relating D2/D3 BP and craving to gray-matter volume, the full text does not present a direct whole-brain between-group contrast (substance users vs. controls) of GM volume. The analyses focus on group-by-receptor interactions and within-group correlations rather than a main effect GM comparison between users and controls. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3 (requirement for at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast), although it satisfies I2, I4 and I5. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing smokers (nicotine-dependent individuals) to nonsmoking controls. The paper reports voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts with FDR-corrected results and provides peak coordinates/tables and figures (Table 2, Figures 1–2). The authors also performed a whole-brain DARTEL analysis (reported in Supplementary Materials) and provide sufficient methodological detail (participant age/sex, FTND scores, scanner field strength 3.0T, preprocessing and statistical software: SPM8, SUIT, DARTEL, DPARSFA). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses or non-empirical report) apply. The full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using deformation-based morphometry to compare recovering alcohol-dependent participants to light-drinking controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise (DBM) between-group contrasts (cross-sectional and longitudinal), including cluster-level results and descriptions of affected GM regions, and provides participant demographics, MRI acquisition, and preprocessing/statistical methods. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for whole-brain GM comparisons and provides adequate methodological and participant detail. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing substance-dependent individuals (poly-substance: cocaine, amphetamine, alcohol) versus healthy controls. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts with family-wise error cluster-level correction and provides voxel coordinates (e.g., MNI −5,53,−3) confirming voxelwise results. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (including duration of abstinence), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5.1, SPM5) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users versus controls.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed human structural MRI study of amphetamine-dependent patients vs healthy controls that evaluates cortical grey matter (cortical thickness) across the whole cortical mantle using vertex-wise (whole-brain) analyses (FreeSurfer) with multiple-comparison control (FDR). Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use history, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Results include whole-brain between-group contrasts (maps/figures) comparing users to controls, and follow-up contrasts addressing alcohol comorbidity. Although the primary metric is cortical thickness rather than voxelwise GM volume/density, cortical thickness is a valid whole-brain structural grey-matter measure relevant to the meta-analysis objective (structurally altered GM regions in substance users). Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volumes between detoxified alcohol-dependent subjects and healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with peak coordinates and tables/figures, describes MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2), and participant demographics (age, male-only). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References).

This is an empirical English-language MRI VBM study of smokers vs never-smokers and reports voxelwise cerebellar coordinates and methodological details, but the analysis is restricted to the cerebellum/brainstem using the SUIT toolbox (i.e., a region-focused, infratentorial mask) rather than a whole-brain GM volume contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports only region-of-interest/infratentorial analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences), I4 (voxelwise result reported as coordinates/figures), I5 (participant and MRI/preprocessing/statistical details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude under E5.

The study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI investigation comparing substance-dependent individuals (SDI) and controls using FreeSurfer and reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software (satisfies I2 and I5). The paper also presents vertex-wise whole-brain maps for cortical thickness (figures/trends), so voxelwise results are shown visually (I4). However, the manuscript does not report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast of grey matter volume (e.g., VBM-style GM volume/density/concentration) comparing substance users versus controls. Volume comparisons were reported primarily as region-of-interest analyses; no qualifying whole-brain GM volume results are provided. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Accordingly, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry that compares gray matter between 20 alcohol-dependent patients and 20 controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts using SPM2 with thresholding and describes significant clusters/regions (tables/figures). Participant characteristics (male, age-matched), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing alcohol-dependent (AD) subjects (N=119) to matched healthy controls (N=97). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (controls > AD) with whole-brain univariate analyses, t-maps (figures), and supplementary tables of regional results. Participant demographics (age ranges, sex counts), substance-use measures (lifetime consumption), MRI field strength and acquisition parameters (3T Siemens Trio, MPRAGE details), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, VBM8) are all reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; empirical human data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract this is an empirical 1.5T MRI study reporting gray matter volume deficits in alcoholic patients vs controls, so I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison) is met. However, I cannot confirm whether at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast (I3) is reported, nor whether coordinate tables/figures for voxelwise results are available (I4). Reporting of participant details and preprocessing/software is incomplete in the abstract (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5/E6) are clearly met. Because the full text is not available to verify whole-brain results and requisite detail, I must exclude this study pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of adolescents with alcohol use disorder vs controls that reports hippocampal (ROI) volumetry and overall tissue volumes, and it reports participant ages, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical tools (FMRIB FAST, AFNI). However, the paper does not present any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrasts — analyses and results are ROI-based (manual hippocampal tracings) and global tissue-volume comparisons only. Per the review criteria, studies that report only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results must be excluded (E5). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing adolescent smokers to nonsmoker controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reporting significant GMV differences (vmPFC) with cluster coordinates and statistics. The paper reports participant age (14-year-olds), demographic info, smoking exposure measures, MRI field strength (3T across sites), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8 for VBM; FSL for DTI). Whole-brain GM analyses and coordinate/cluster results are clearly presented; voxelwise results are reported with coordinates and corrected cluster thresholds. The study addresses nicotine use and meets the review objective. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI mega-analysis reporting gray matter differences between substance-dependent individuals and nondependent controls across many whole-brain FreeSurfer-defined regions (82 ROIs). The full text includes introduction, methods (T1 acquisition, FreeSurfer v5.3 preprocessing, statistical modeling), results (whole-brain ROI comparisons, cross-validation), and discussion. Participant age/sex and substance characteristics and scanner/acquisition details are reported (main text and supplement). Thus it meets inclusion criteria for empirical MRI GM volume comparisons (I2), reports whole-brain between-group contrasts across the brain via comprehensive ROI analyses (I3), and provides key participant and methods details (I5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-limited without whole-brain results, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of cocaine users versus controls that performed voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences) and I5 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software). However, the paper reports that whole-brain VBM between-group analyses were nonsignificant and therefore provides no qualifying whole-brain coordinates of GM differences; instead, the authors conducted post-hoc ROI analyses (based on fMRI peaks) and report an rACC ROI effect. Because there are no significant whole-brain GM between-group results to include and the reported structural finding is ROI-based, this meets exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM contrast with significant peaks). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter density between cocaine users (a stimulant) and matched nondrug-using controls. The full text provides whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (tables and figures of significant clusters), reports participant demographics (age/sex), substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of substance-related GM alterations.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing regular cannabis users and occasional users (controls). Methods report whole-brain two-sample voxelwise contrasts with SPM8, DARTEL registration, modulation, smoothing, and FWE-corrected statistics; results report significant between-group whole-brain clusters (coordinates and cluster descriptions) and voxelwise correlations with usage frequency. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics details are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons relevant to cannabis.

This study is excluded because it reports ROI/parcellation-based FreeSurfer analyses and tests associations between a continuous alcohol index within a community twin sample rather than presenting whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group contrasts comparing substance users to controls. Exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criterion I5 is satisfied (participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). Inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (reports at least one whole-brain between-group contrast comparing substance users vs controls) are not met. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter concentration between MDMA (a stimulant-class drug) polydrug users and non-MDMA controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (SPM/VBM) with corrected and uncorrected thresholds and describes affected regions; methods report participant age/sex, drug-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although participants are polydrug users, the study meets the review’s inclusion requirements for whole-brain GM comparisons in the stimulant class.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter (GMD) between heroin-dependent (opioid) users and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (ANOVA on modulated gray matter segments) and provides coordinate/region-level results (frontal, cingulate, occipital reductions). Key methodological details are reported: participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (GE Signa 1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, VBM). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and therefore is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Study is directly relevant to the opioid class in the meta-analysis and meets inclusion criteria I2–I5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter density between 63 opiate-dependent subjects and 46 matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (VBM) with corrected statistical thresholds and presents regional results in text/tables and figures (prefrontal, insular, temporal GM decreases). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (including methadone treatment and comorbid substance history), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99, VBM procedures) are described. The study is not an ROI-only analysis nor a non-empirical paper. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cortical grey matter volumes between methamphetamine-dependent users (n=34) and non-user controls (n=31). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. MRI acquisition (3.0T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL for segmentation; SAS for stats) are reported, and participant demographics, age/sex, and substance-use characteristics are detailed. The study performed whole-brain regional analyses by segmenting the entire cortex into six main lobes and 17 subregions (whole-brain coverage) and conducted between-group contrasts (ANCOVA, repeated-measures ANCOVA) comparing GM volumes between users and controls, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain between-group GM comparisons. Coordinate tables/voxelwise maps are not necessary per I4 since whole-brain ROI-based contrasts are reported in the main text/tables. The study pertains to a stimulant (methamphetamine), matching the meta-analysis objective. Full text appears complete.

Empirical structural MRI study of prenatal cocaine exposure (a stimulant) comparing grey matter volumes between exposed children and non-exposed controls using whole-brain automated segmentation (FreeSurfer). Reports between-group comparisons of cortical gray matter and multiple subcortical structures (thalamus, putamen, etc.), with subject ages/sex, exposure characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software described. This constitutes whole-brain volumetric evidence rather than an ROI-only study. Therefore it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for studies assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter volume between chronic cocaine users (stimulant class) and healthy controls. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (CUD vs CON) with voxelwise results presented in tables and figures, specifies MRI field strength (4 Tesla), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5.1), and provides participant demographics (male, ages) and detailed substance-use characteristics (years of cocaine, alcohol, smoking). The study is not ROI-only and contains original data. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of cocaine users vs controls that reports cortical thickness differences (FreeSurfer) and provides participant and MRI details. However, the imaging analysis is restricted to ROI-based and mean cortical-thickness measures (frontal ROIs and whole-brain mean thickness) rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast with stereotactic coordinates. No whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise results or coordinate tables/figures are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion I2 and I5 but does not meet I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast) nor I4 (voxelwise coordinate reporting). It is excluded under E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that compares adolescents who initiated heavy/moderate alcohol use to a no/low-drinking control group. The paper reports whole-brain analyses using FreeSurfer cortical parcellation (34 bilateral ROIs covering the cortex) and lobar ROIs with between-group contrasts and multiple-comparison correction (FDR/Bonferroni) identifying regions with steeper gray matter declines in heavy drinkers (e.g., frontal, caudal middle frontal, superior frontal, posterior cingulate). Participant age/sex and detailed substance-use measures are reported; MRI preprocessing software (FreeSurfer) and acquisition procedures are described. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2 and I3 (whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing nicotine-dependent smokers to nonsmoking controls (meets I2). The paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses with voxelwise group contrasts and coordinates, including corrected peak p-values (meets I3 and I4). Participant demographics (age, sex), smoking characteristics (cigarettes/day, pack-years), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (MEDx, SPM99, smoothing kernel) are reported (meets I5). No exclusion criteria apply: the study includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only, so E5 not met) and is empirical (E6 not met). Full text appears complete with background, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing methamphetamine-dependent (stimulant) users to control groups (I2). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (ANCOVA and post-hoc t-tests) and longitudinal whole-brain analyses (I3); voxelwise results are described in the main text and clusters reported, satisfying acceptability for coordinate/voxelwise reporting (I4). Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8, DARTEL) are reported (I5). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only study (E5) nor non-empirical (E6). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of adolescents with alcohol use disorder vs matched controls that reports whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (FSL-VBM) showing significant GM density differences and confirms findings with ROI analyses. The manuscript provides participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FIRST, FAST, SIENAX), satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of substance-related GM differences.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (VBM analyses) with family-wise error correction and provides regional results (figures and tables with coordinates). Participant characteristics (sex, drinking history), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM pipeline) are described. It is not ROI-only and contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing daily cannabis users to nonusers with voxelwise whole-brain analyses (VBM and FreeSurfer whole-brain GLMs) of gray matter volume/density and shape. The paper reports participant demographics (age/sex counts), substance-use measures, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSLVBM, FreeSurfer, FIRST). Whole-brain contrasts were explicitly performed and reported (though null), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical).

This is a human postmortem pathological volumetric study (high-resolution computerized counts of tissue sections), not an in vivo MRI study. It reports region-of-interest (ACC, insula, thalamus, DLPFC and subregions) volumetry and explicitly lacks any whole-brain voxelwise MRI contrasts or coordinate-based results. Therefore it does not meet the MRI-based inclusion requirements and qualifies for exclusion. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain MRI results). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (empirical MRI study), I3 (whole-brain between-group MRI contrast), I4 (no voxelwise/coordinate whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (VBM) comparing heavy smokers (n=16) to matched non-smoker controls and reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses with stereotactic coordinates. The paper provides between-group GM contrasts (VBM) and reports MNI coordinates for GM reductions in bilateral cerebellar tonsil (with small-volume correction) and describes whole-brain thresholding procedures; demographic, substance-use (cigarettes/day, years, FTND), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, PROBID for SVM) are reported. Voxelwise results are given in-text with coordinates and figures. Although some GM results are reported with small-volume correction, the study conducted whole-brain VBM and provides qualifying voxelwise results; therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E5/E6).

The study reports original human structural MRI data using voxel-based morphometry comparing 20 synthetic cannabinoid users to 20 healthy controls and reports between-group voxelwise gray matter differences (reduced GM in bilateral thalamus and left cerebellum). Based on the abstract and available content, it satisfies: I2 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I3 (whole-brain voxelwise VBM results reported), and I4 (voxelwise results are clearly reported in the text/abstract). The full text provided here is incomplete (only abstract/metadata/references present), so MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software could not be confirmed and some methodological details are missing; additionally, there is some uncertainty whether 'synthetic cannabinoids' should be grouped within the review's 'cannabis' class. Therefore inclusion is recommended but with moderate confidence and fulltext_incomplete=true.

The study is excluded because it reports ROI-based analyses limited to 24 preselected ‘cue reactivity’ regions rather than providing a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language human MRI study assessing GM volume differences between heavy drinkers and light-drinker controls) and I5 (reports participant ages/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/VBM8/DARTEL)). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain evidence, this paper does not qualify despite relevant findings on alcohol-related GM differences in adolescents, particularly because the analyses are constrained to ROIs only.

E5 met: The study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics and MRI parameters (meets I5). However, all reported analyses focus on cerebellar lobular parcellation and regional volumetry (ROI-based analyses) rather than reporting any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast (no VBM or whole-brain SPM-style results), so it does not meet I3. Therefore it must be excluded under exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey-matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (VBM/2-sample t-test) and reporting voxelwise regression results. The paper reports whole-brain GM between-group contrasts (FDR-corrected clusters) and voxelwise longitudinal Jacobian analyses, with results presented in text and figures. Participant demographics (n, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5, SPM5, TBM methods) are described or referenced. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM structural comparisons in alcohol users versus controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (SPM99) to compare gray matter concentration between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients (n=13) and controls (n=16). It reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (corrected results, p<.01) and gives participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey-matter volume between chronic synthetic cannabinoid (SC) users and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group SnPM VBM results (significant clusters in right frontal lobe) and also provides ROI analyses; voxelwise results and coordinates are described/mentioned. Participant demographics (male, ages reported), substance-use characteristics (SC use duration and detected compounds listed in appendix), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, SnPM) are reported. These satisfy inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; study is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, limitations, appendix). Therefore include for meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users vs. controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using optimized whole-brain VBM to compare gray matter volumes between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) subjects and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (SPM2 results, corrected p-values, coordinates and figures), provides participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software details. Results include voxelwise tables/figures and coordinate reporting for significant GM volume differences. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective (stimulants) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (DARTEL-based VBM) comparing smokers and age-matched non-smokers. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (smokers vs non-smokers) with AlphaSim-corrected voxelwise results and region coordinates/tables referenced, and also reports correlations with lifetime tobacco consumption (pack-years). Participant characteristics (all male, ages 23–40), substance-use measures (cigarettes/day, years, pack-years, light vs heavy groups), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are described. Thus it satisfies I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain voxelwise contrasts), I4 (results reported in figures/tables), and I5 (key methodological/participant details provided). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s primary inclusion requirements for grey-matter (GM) volume voxelwise comparisons. Although it is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of substance-using adolescents with full methods and results (ages/sex reported; 3T scanner; FreeSurfer preprocessing) and reports whole-cerebrum vertex-wise cortical-thickness analyses (including cluster coordinates), it assesses cortical thickness rather than grey-matter volume/density/concentration. Therefore: inclusion met: I4 (voxelwise/vertex results reported) and I5 (participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength and software are reported). Inclusion NOT met: I2 (study does NOT assess GM volume/density/concentration) and I3 (whole-brain contrasts reported are for cortical thickness, not GM volume). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Given the meta-analysis objective (GM volume differences across substance classes), this paper must be excluded.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between former heroin-dependent individuals and matched controls. It reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (VBM two-sample t-test) with corrected results and provides peak MNI coordinates for clusters of reduced GM. Participant demographics, substance-use history (duration, abstinence), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing alcoholic patients (substance users) with healthy controls, reporting whole-brain between-group contrasts and voxelwise results in tables/figures. Participant age/sex, alcohol use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T GE Discovery), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CAT12) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only (E5) nor non-empirical (E6). Full text appears complete (supplementary material referenced but not required).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing substance-using groups (alcohol-dependent only and polysubstance) to healthy controls and reports subcortical and global gray-matter measurements and relevant participant/MRI details (inclusion criteria met: I2, I5). However, the paper presents region-based subcortical volumetric (FIRST) and summary tissue-volume analyses (ROI/segmentations) and does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast (no VBM or coordinate tables/whole-brain statistical maps). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group GM contrast) is not met (I4 likewise not applicable). Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI VBM study of cocaine use disorder comparing users and controls (I2 satisfied). However, the manuscript does NOT report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls; group comparisons were conducted using predefined bilateral rACC ROIs and ROI-based VBM, and the authors explicitly state they did not perform whole-brain group difference analyses. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using optimized voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter (GM) volume between heroin-dependent (opioid) subjects and matched healthy controls. It performs a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast and reports significant GM volume reductions (right PFC, left SMC, bilateral cingulate) with cluster-level statistics and references to table/figure results. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics (duration, dose, route, nicotine use), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM2/SPM2, ANCOVA) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports only ROI-based subcortical volumetric analyses (seven predefined subcortical ROIs) and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text is available and complete for assessment.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing nicotine-dependent smokers to age- and gender-matched non-smokers with whole-brain between-group contrasts reported (cluster- and voxel-level results, tables/figures with MNI coordinates). Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use measures (years smoked, cigarettes/day, FTND, pack-years), MRI field strength (3T Siemens TIM Trio), and preprocessing/statistical software (DARTEL, SPM8, MATLAB) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the nicotine (tobacco) class and should be included.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of alcohol users vs controls that reports cerebellar grey- and white-matter volumes using manual parcellation and provides participant demographics and MRI details (I2 and I5 are satisfied). However, the paper does not report a whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group contrast of grey matter volume; analyses are limited to cerebellar parcellation/ROI-based volumes (no qualifying whole-brain GM contrast). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for the cerebellar-focused study (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey matter volumes between occasional amphetamine-type stimulant/cocaine users (N=165) and stimulant-naïve controls (N=48). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group analyses (linear mixed effects model) and whole-brain regressions relating lifetime use to regional GM volume, with coordinates and cluster results described. Methods report participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FNIRT, FLIRT, AFNI, R). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) performed at 3.0 T that reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons of grey matter volumes between alcohol use disorder (AUD) participants and healthy controls, and also reports comparisons involving problem gamblers. The methods section describes MRI acquisition, preprocessing (SPM8, DARTEL), statistical analysis (whole-brain FDR correction), and participant demographics (male-only sample, ages, AUDIT scores, abstinence duration, smoking status), satisfying reporting expectations. The paper clearly provides whole-brain voxelwise results (significant clusters reported and visualized) comparing substance users (alcohol) vs controls. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (VBM) comparing grey matter between alcohol users and healthy controls. It reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (VBM) with cluster-corrected results and provides coordinate-based correlational analyses. Key study details are reported: participant demographics (age range, all male), substance-use characteristics (DSM-IV alcohol abuse, years and amount of use), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5, detailed pipeline). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations.

Full text reports an empirical VBM study of cocaine-dependent individuals vs controls (meets I2) and provides participant details and MRI methods (meets I5). However, all between-group voxelwise comparisons were conducted using an ROI/SVC approach and no whole-brain between-group GM contrast (with reported coordinates or clusters) is presented; significant results are reported only for within-group (severity-related) correlations and ROI analyses. Therefore the study reports only ROI-based voxelwise results with no qualifying whole-brain between-group findings, violating inclusion criterion I3 and meeting exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study with complete full text reporting introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports whole-brain cortical thickness analyses (FreeSurfer, 3.0T) across parcellated cortical regions and provides participant age/sex and substance-use details (satisfying I5). However, the meta-analysis inclusion requires studies assessing grey matter (GM) volume/density/concentration differences (I2). This study reports cortical thickness measures rather than GM volume/density/concentration, so it does not meet I2. Therefore it must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered by this paper; full text is complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients and matched controls. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, MRI acquisition at 3T, preprocessing with SPM8/DARTEL), Results (voxel-wise two-sample t-tests with cluster correction) and Discussion. Whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts are reported (figures and cluster results described), and participant demographics and imaging parameters are provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey matter density between cigarette smokers (nicotine users) and never-smokers. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (VBM whole-brain independent-samples t-tests) with cluster-level coordinates and figures, and provides participant demographics, smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8/SPM8, FreeSurfer, ANTS). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis objective (nicotine class). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of heavy cannabis users reporting cortical morphology (thickness, gray–white contrast, gyrification) using whole-brain vertex-wise analyses. However, the study does not include a healthy control group and does not report any whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring direct GM comparisons between users and controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I2 (no empirical GM volume differences reported between substance users and controls), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language VBM study of heroin-dependent men providing voxelwise coordinates and full methodological details. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI VBM study), I4 (voxelwise coordinates reported), I5 (participant age/sex, substance use, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). However, the reported GMV difference was identified using small-volume correction within a predefined DLPFC ROI and no whole-brain corrected between-group GMV result is reported; thus the study effectively reports only ROI findings. Inclusion criterion I3 (report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume) is not met. This violates exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between individuals with cocaine use disorder (stimulant users) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (including cluster coordinates, sizes and corrected p-values) and a between-group contrast (controls > CUD) for the mid-cingulate cortex, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, and it is empirical human MRI work). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and Conclusions.

This study is an empirical 3T structural MRI investigation of nicotine-dependent smokers vs nonsmokers and reports GM volume analyses focused on insular subregions (anterior/posterior insula) and seed-based structural covariance. It does not present a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast of GM volume with reported coordinates or cluster results comparing substance users vs controls. Therefore it meets exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing GM between users and controls) and I5 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI investigation using optimized voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter density between lifetime heroin-dependent individuals and matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts demonstrating decreased gray matter density in multiple regions (prefrontal, anterior cingulate, temporal, insula, cerebellum) and presents correlation analyses with duration of heroin use. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (duration, abstinence, nicotine/alcohol info), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM2, SPM2, MATLAB) are described. This is not an ROI-only study or a non-empirical paper. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing grey matter volume between binge-drinking alcohol users and matched controls. The paper reports both ROI and an exploratory whole-brain between-group analysis (whole-brain results reported at P<0.001 uncorrected with coordinates/clusters), and provides coordinate tables/figures and correlation analyses. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8) are reported. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for alcohol studies with voxelwise whole-brain GM contrasts and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between stimulant-dependent patients and matched healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (two-way ANCOVA, FWE cluster-corrected) with figures and coordinates, as well as ROI cross-validation. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8) are reported. The study is not ROI-only and is original human MRI data. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent participants and controls (meets I2). The paper reports participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing/statistical methods (3T scanner, ANTs/FSL/FreeSurfer, etc.), satisfying I5. However, the analyses are atlas/parcellation-based regional (lobar and frontal subregions) ROI volume comparisons rather than voxel-wise whole-brain between-group contrasts with coordinate-based results. The study does not present qualifying whole‑brain voxelwise contrasts/tables of coordinates required by I3. Therefore it is excluded under E5 (ROI-only analyses). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing female adolescent substance users with severe substance and conduct problems (patients, n=22) to controls (n=21) using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses. The manuscript reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (controls>patients) with clusterwise results and figures, uses SPM8/VBM8/DARTEL preprocessing on 3T MRI data, and provides participant age range, sex, substance use diagnoses, and imaging parameters. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2 (empirical English-language MRI GM volume comparison), I3 (reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts), I4 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), and I5 (reports age/sex, substance characteristics, field strength, and preprocessing/software). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM study of cocaine (stimulant) users and controls (meets I2). It reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics (meets I5). However, the primary voxelwise analyses are within the abstinent cocaine group (regressions of GM against weeks abstinent and years of use). The paper does not report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group (substance users vs controls) contrast; comparisons to controls were performed post-hoc on extracted ROIs (Welch t-tests), i.e. ROI-based tests rather than a qualifying whole-brain between-group analysis. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI/no qualifying whole-brain between-group results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM study comparing college-aged binge drinkers (substance users: alcohol) to healthy volunteers (controls). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group analyses (cluster- and voxel-level FWE results) and provides peak MNI coordinates and cluster sizes (e.g., ventral striatum MNI coordinates, Z and FWE P-values). Participant demographics (age, sex distribution), substance-use characteristics (binge criteria, AUDIT scores), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of grey matter differences in substance (alcohol) users versus controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing methamphetamine-dependent (stimulant) participants to controls (2x2 design including HIV and METH factors). The paper reports whole-cortex analyses using Freesurfer parcellation (Desikan-Killiany atlas) with ROI-wise between-group contrasts across all 68 cortical ROIs, and reports cortical volume (and thickness/area) group differences and corrected results. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer v5.3.0) are provided. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain between-group contrasts via whole-cortex ROI analysis), I4 (results reported in text/tables/figures), and I5 (key sample and MRI details reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only limited to a small region; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study (PLOS One, 2016) comparing alcohol-dependent patients (n=20) with healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reporting whole-brain between-group GMV contrasts. Methods report MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL), participant demographics and substance-use characteristics, and voxelwise results (peak clusters, figures/tables). The study addresses alcohol (one of the target drug classes) and provides whole-brain coordinate-based results linking GMV reductions to impulsivity. All required inclusion criteria are met (I2, I3, I4, I5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of cocaine users vs controls that reports cortical and subcortical grey-matter measures (cortical thickness, cortical surface area, and subcortical volumes) and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, MAGeTbrain). Thus it meets I2 and I5. However, analyses were restricted to a priori frontal regions-of-interest (six ROIs) and subcortical structures; the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain GM volume between-group contrasts. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion IDs met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I2, I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (whole-brain results).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study of cocaine-dependent individuals vs controls (meets I2). The report provides voxelwise OFC results and figures (meets I4) and reports participant characteristics and preprocessing/software (meets I5). However, the analyses were constrained to an a priori orbitofrontal cortex region and the paper focuses on OFC voxelwise/regressions and OFC volume comparisons; no whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast of substance users vs controls is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Exclusion: E5. Included criteria met: I2, I4, I5. Inclusion criterion not met: I3.

This is an empirical longitudinal structural MRI study of alcohol exposure in college students, but it does not report a whole‑brain between-group comparison of substance users vs. controls. Instead, the authors report voxelwise associations within a hippocampus/parahippocampus mask (ROI-based longitudinal associations with a continuous alcohol-use index). Therefore it violates E5 (ROI-only/no qualifying whole-brain between-group results). It does satisfy I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI acquisition details, preprocessing and software). It does NOT satisfy I2 (no case-control GM volume comparison of substance users vs controls) and I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete. Exclusion ID met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I2, I3 (also I4 not applicable because voxelwise results are within an ROI mask rather than whole-brain between-group results).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing young adult recreational cannabis users (n=20) to matched controls (n=20) using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (gray matter density), regional volume, and shape analyses. The paper reports whole-brain VBM contrasts with voxelwise cluster results (Tables/Figures) and provides participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FreeSurfer). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I2,I3,I4,I5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears to include Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) to compare gray matter volume (GMV) between cocaine users and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (non-parametric permutation testing with TFCE) and regional correlations with abstinence duration; results are described in the main text (and coordinate/cluster detail implied). Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, Randomise, FNIRT, etc.) are reported. The substance class (stimulant: cocaine) fits the review scope. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports structural MRI in 60 alcohol-dependent subjects with FreeSurfer segmentation and relates gray-matter volumes to executive performance, but it does not include a control group or any between-group (substance users vs. controls) whole-brain contrast. Therefore it does not meet the review's requirement for between-group GM comparisons. Exclusion rationale: No qualifying whole-brain between-group results reported. Inclusion/exclusion summary provided below.

Full text is complete. This study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI paper comparing alcohol use disorder (AUD) patients to controls and reports whole-brain surface-based cortical thickness (CT) contrasts and tables/figures. However, the review’s inclusion I2 specifically requires assessment of grey matter (GM) volume differences (e.g., volume, density, or concentration). This study reports cortical thickness measures (surface-based morphometry) rather than voxelwise GM volume/density/concentration (VBM-style) metrics requested by the meta-analysis. Therefore it does not meet I2 and cannot be included. It does meet I3 (whole-brain between-group contrasts reported), I4 (whole-brain voxelwise/cluster results presented in tables/figures), and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance characteristics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are invoked. Exclusion is based on failure to satisfy inclusion criterion I2 (GM volume/density/concentration metric).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cortical gray matter volumes between chronic alcoholic men and healthy controls. The authors measured cortical gray matter (defined across the cortical mantle) and reported between-group contrasts and changes over time, satisfying whole-brain GM comparison requirements rather than an ROI-only approach. Participant demographic and substance-use information (age range, male sex, lifetime alcohol consumption) and MRI acquisition parameters (sequence details, TR/TE, FOV, matrix) are reported; although scanner field strength and voxelwise coordinate tables are not provided, the protocol and regional volumetric results meet the meta-analysis’ acceptable reporting standards and missing single items do not mandate exclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not a review). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Recommended for inclusion for analyses of alcohol-related GM differences.

The provided “full text” is only an HTML skeleton without the article’s introduction, methods, results, or discussion. I cannot confirm this is an empirical structural MRI study comparing grey matter between methamphetamine users and controls or verify whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts. Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (cannot verify MRI GM comparisons), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts reported in the text provided), I4 (no voxelwise coordinates/figures available), I5 (participant and MRI/method details missing).
