No explicit exclusion criteria (E5/E6) are met from the available content, but full text is incomplete so review criteria cannot be applied. Excluding for inability to assess eligibility due to incomplete full text.

Full text appears to be limited to title/abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). The study examines adolescents with heavy prenatal alcohol exposure (not current substance users), so it does not meet inclusion criterion I2 (between substance users and controls). The abstract indicates surface-based whole-brain maps of gray matter asymmetry (I3 met), and mentions traditional volumetric ROI analyses; however, without the full text I cannot verify voxelwise whole-brain GM volume contrasts or full methodological details. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are explicitly met (E5 and E6 not applicable). Therefore, exclude due to failure to meet I2 and incomplete full text preventing confirmation of other required details.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcoholic patients and matched control subjects with quantitative measures of cortical gray matter and CSF volumes over time. The methods describe whole-brain segmentation across seven axial slices sampling approximately half the brain and report global cortical gray matter and regional cortical volumes and group-by-time contrasts between alcohol users and controls. Participant age ranges, drinking behavior, scanner field strength (1.5 T), and image-processing/statistical approaches are reported. The paper therefore provides whole-brain (global and regionally parcellated) GM volume comparisons between substance users (alcohol) and controls and meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent participants to controls and reports participant demographics and MRI details (meets I2 and I5). However, the analyses focus on hippocampal morphometry (region-specific bilateral hippocampal volumes obtained via semi-automated delineation) rather than reporting any whole-brain voxelwise/between-group whole-brain GM contrasts or coordinate-based results. Therefore it does not meet the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and qualifies as an ROI-only study with no qualifying whole-brain results (meets exclusion E5). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to E5 (ROI-only); inclusion met: I2 and I5; inclusion not met: I3.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing heroin-dependent individuals (n=24) to matched controls (n=24). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (decreased GM volume in bilateral medial PFC, bilateral DLPFC, right fusiform) with multiple-comparison correction (FDR) and cluster thresholds; voxelwise results are described and supplementary material with tables/figures is indicated. Participant demographics (group sizes, sex), substance-use characteristics (heroin dependence, duration, methadone maintenance), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5.1, SPM5, MATLAB) are provided. The study is neither ROI-only nor non-empirical. Core article sections (intro, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study was excluded because it does not assess grey-matter volume/density/concentration using whole-brain voxelwise GM volume contrasts as required. Instead, it reports cortical thickness measures (insula thickness and vertex-wise thickness analyses) rather than GM volume/density, and the primary analyses are ROI-based for the insula. Although whole-brain vertex-wise thickness analyses were performed, they are not qualifying whole-brain GM volume contrasts as specified by the inclusion criteria. Therefore inclusion criteria I2 (GM volume/density/concentration measure) and I3 (whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast) are not met. The paper does report participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software (satisfying I5). Exclusion criterion E5 applies because no qualifying whole-brain GM volume results are provided.

Although this is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that reports whole-brain voxelwise associations of alcohol use severity with gray matter and provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software, it does not present any whole-brain between-group contrast comparing substance users versus controls. The analyses use a continuous AUDIT severity approach without a separate user vs control group (authors note they did not include a separate control group). Therefore inclusion criteria I2 and I3 are not met. I4 and I5 are satisfied. No listed exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Excluded for failing to meet required between-group comparison criteria for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent subjects (a stimulant class) to non-drug-using controls using voxel-wise methods (TBM and VBM). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group analyses conducted with SPM8 (voxel-wise FWE correction across the whole brain) and presents the null results; therefore whole-brain contrasts of GM volume were performed and are available. Participant demographics, age/gender, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical).

This study reports manual volumetric (ROI) measurements of grey-matter structures (temporal lobe, superior temporal gyrus, hippocampus/amygdala) and DTI voxelwise analyses of FA/ADC (diffusion measures). While it is an empirical MRI study and reports participant demographics and scan parameters (meets I2 and I5), it does NOT report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast of grey-matter volume (no VBM or whole-brain GM volume maps). The voxelwise analyses presented are of diffusion metrics (FA/ADC), not GM volume, and the volumetric results are ROI-based rather than whole-brain voxelwise. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain GM results) and fails inclusion criterion I3 (no whole-brain GM contrast). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with significant GMV cluster coordinates and cluster sizes (reported in text and figures/tables). Participant demographics (right-handed male patients; age-matched controls), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study comparing adolescent binge drinkers to matched non-drinking controls using structural MRI-derived cortical morphometry (cortical thickness) and reports between-group contrasts. The authors performed whole-brain (vertex-wise) analyses in addition to region-wise (FreeSurfer parcellation) analyses and explicitly report results (significant binge×gender interactions localized to left frontal regions; whole-brain search yielded no additional interactions). Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer v5.0, SPSS) are reported. Cortical thickness is a grey-matter structural metric relevant to the meta-analysis objective of identifying structurally altered GM regions. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria and does not meet exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent participants and healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (regions of decreased grey matter volume in alcoholics) with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics, and provides participant demographics (male-only sample, ages), substance-use characteristics (duration, amount, abstinence), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, VBM). Results are reported voxelwise in the main text/figures and regression analyses were performed; this is not an ROI-only or non-empirical paper. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations, conclusion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (combined voxel-wise P<0.001 and cluster-extent thresholds with PFWE<0.05), provides MNI coordinates and cluster sizes in results/tables and figures, and describes participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (VBM8, SPM8). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is empirical, in English, uses VBM whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports necessary participant/MRI/preprocessing details, but it does not report a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users versus controls. Instead, the paper presents whole-brain regression analyses relating number/amount of substances to GM volume across a combined sample. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply.

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses on frontal and temporal lobe slabs (manual tracings over a seven-slice contiguous volume) with no whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, and MRI field strength). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume reported). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not meet the required whole-brain analysis criterion and must be excluded.

This is an empirical, English-language longitudinal MRI study using tensor-based morphometry (voxelwise whole-brain TBM) comparing cannabis users vs non-users and reporting voxelwise between-group contrasts and peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for significant findings. The paper conducted whole-brain analyses (reported, albeit not whole-brain FWE-significant) and supplemented with small-volume-corrected voxelwise results in predefined regions (AHC and frontal lobes) with reported coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, scanner field strength (1-T Siemens), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2/SPM5, TBM protocol) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; empirical data present).

This is an empirical structural MRI VBM study directly comparing smokers (nicotine users) and nonsmoking controls. The study used whole-brain coverage via a 1,024-ROI parcellation of the AAL atlas, performed VBM preprocessing (SPM8/VBM8) on 3T data, and applied multivariate classification to discriminate groups. Results include a map of consistent ROIs (N=150) and a table (Table 2) that lists ROIs with MNI center coordinates and sizes, satisfying the requirement that qualifying voxelwise/coordinate results be available. Participant demographics, smoking measures (FTND, CPD, lifetime usage), scanner field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Although the primary analysis is a multivariate classifier rather than a conventional univariate voxelwise t-contrast, the paper provides whole-brain-derived regional results with coordinates and regression analyses relating GMV to smoking measures, which meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I4; I5 (reporting details) is also satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded per E5: the study reports voxel‑based morphometry results restricted to nine a priori ROIs (WFU PickAtlas masks) rather than reporting an unmasked whole‑brain voxelwise between‑group contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM differences between cocaine-dependent participants and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength [3T], and preprocessing/statistical software [SPM2]). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no qualifying whole‑brain between-group voxelwise contrast is reported; analyses were ROI-constrained) and I4 (no unmasked whole‑brain voxelwise coordinates/figures of between-group results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients (substance users) and age-/gender-matched healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (One-Way ANCOVA and post-hoc tests) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides methodological details (participant demographics, 3T MRI field strength, CAT12/SPM12 preprocessing and statistical software). Results are reported in main text and supplementary tables. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because the VBM analyses reported were performed using region-of-interest (ROI) masks derived from the AAL atlas (left lateral frontal, parietal, temporal lobes, hippocampus) rather than reporting a whole-brain between-group (AUD vs. control) voxelwise contrast meeting the review’s whole-brain requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing GM between substance users and controls), I4 (voxelwise results/coordinates are reported/quoted in the text/tables), and I5 (participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no clear whole-brain between-group contrast reported). Exclusion criteria applied: E5 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete and contains background, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

E5: Study reports only region-based volumetric analyses (Freesurfer segmentation of subcortical structures and global brain volumes) and regression/group comparisons, but does not report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast (e.g., VBM or SPM voxelwise results). Inclusion met: I2 (empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing smokers vs controls on GM/brain volumes) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, smoking characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion not met: I3 (no whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter density between nicotine-dependent smokers and matched non-smoking controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (FWE-corrected VBM results) and provides coordinate/cluster results for left insula and left PFC. Participant demographics, substance-use measures (pack-years, FTND), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, IRG registration, AFNI, etc.) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for GM whole-brain structural comparisons in nicotine users vs controls.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent individuals (stimulant class) with healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts, cluster-level results and regional coordinates/figures, and describes participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSLVBM, CamBA). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; original human data). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent participants to healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (SPM8/DARTEL). The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts with cluster results, MNI/Talairach coordinates, figures, and ROC analyses (satisfying voxelwise reporting). Participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI acquisition (high-resolution T1 parameters), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; it's original human MRI data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients to healthy controls. The full text reports whole-brain, voxelwise GMV analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and presents anatomical localization (figures and tables/coordinates), MRI acquisition parameters (MPRAGE, TR/TE/voxel size), and preprocessing/statistical software details (SPM8, New Segment, DARTEL). Participant age/sex and substance-use characteristics are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between chronic cocaine users and matched healthy controls. The paper reports voxelwise VBM analyses (whole-brain processing described) and presents between-group contrasts with coordinates (referenced Tables/Figures) showing reduced VMPFC gray matter in CUD (ROI-corrected FWE) and notes whole-brain results (no other clusters survived whole-brain correction). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8) are reported. Thus it satisfies I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only without whole-brain analyses; not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry comparing methamphetamine-dependent users (n=30) at 6 months' abstinence with drug-naïve controls (n=27), and a longitudinal within-subject comparison to 12 months. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (significance threshold p<0.001, FWE cluster-corrected p<0.05) and regional findings in the main text, and provides participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing whole-brain gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent (stimulant) patients and matched controls. The Methods report a whole-brain between-groups VBM analysis with results (greater GM volume in right caudate and right orbitofrontal gyri) presented in figures/tables. MRI field strength (3 T) and preprocessing/statistical approaches are described (with supporting information). The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I3 (whole-brain between-group VBM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), and I5 (participant demographics, substance-use details, MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistics provided). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed English-language structural MRI study comparing subjects with alcohol use disorder (AUD) to matched controls. It reports whole-brain analyses of gray matter (volumetric and surface-based cortical thickness) using FreeSurfer/Qdec with appropriate multiple-comparison correction and presents between-group voxelwise/surface-wise results. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics (age, sex, smoking status, current alcohol consumption, duration) and MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons in substance users (alcohol) and has no exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter and white matter tissue density between heavy cannabis users (n=11) and non-using controls (n=8). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (with cluster-level correction) and provides MNI coordinates for significant GM clusters (including hippocampal small-volume results). MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM99 and VBM procedures), participant sex and substance-use characteristics are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although sample size is small and all participants are male, the study meets inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM volume/density comparisons and reports coordinate-based voxelwise results, so it is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. This is an empirical VBM study with whole-brain between-group contrasts and adequate reporting of demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing (SPM12). However, the primary between-group comparisons are former regular users (FRUs) versus former light users (FLUs) rather than substance users versus non-user healthy controls. The meta-analysis requires studies comparing substance users to controls; here the ‘control’ group consists of light/former users and subjects who never used substances were excluded from analyses. Therefore inclusion criterion I2 is not met, so the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5).

This is an empirical human MRI study that includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing gray matter volume between cocaine use disorder (CUD) participants and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain 2 (Diagnosis) × 2 (PENK) ANCOVA VBM results with cluster-corrected thresholds and identifies a significant Diagnosis × PENK interaction in right inferior frontal gyrus gray matter volume, indicating whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM differences. MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8, SPM8), and substance-use/sample characteristics and demographic covariates are described in the methods. Therefore inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM group comparison), I3 (whole-brain between-group voxelwise GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures/tables), and I5 (reporting of key methodological/participant details) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (VBM) study comparing grey matter volume between heavy cannabis users (n=33) and matched controls (n=42). The paper reports voxelwise between-group VBM contrasts (whole-brain analysis with a priori ROI masks and thresholds for whole-brain findings) and within-group voxelwise regressions relating GM volume to cannabis use measures. Participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users vs controls.

This article is a narrative/review-style summary of prior MRI studies of prenatal alcohol exposure rather than an original empirical structural MRI study reporting new human voxelwise whole-brain GM between-group contrasts or coordinate tables. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original human structural MRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an empirical MRI study reporting original GM volume differences between substance users and controls), I3 (no original whole-brain between-group GM contrast data presented), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise coordinate tables/figures of original results provided in this paper), I5 (as an overview it does not present a single study’s participant-level age/sex, MRI field strength, or preprocessing/statistical software as required for inclusion). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods summary, results, discussion). Thus the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group ANCOVA results (SPM5) with family-wise error correction and mentions MNI coordinates converted to Talairach, and extracts regional volumes for follow-up analyses. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM) are provided. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study comparing gray matter measures between alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls (meets I2). The paper reports hippocampal GM volume estimates (Hipp/TIV ratio and anterodorsal hippocampal ROI volumes) derived from voxel-based morphometry and uses SPM8 (meets I5). However, it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts or provide whole-brain coordinate tables/figures for GM differences between substance users and controls. The analyses and results are focused on hippocampal/ROI measures rather than qualifying whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing 22 alcohol-dependent patients to 22 matched healthy controls with whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts. The paper reports whole-brain GM and WM differences (tables/figures), provides participant age/sex and substance-use details (duration and daily consumption), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (optimised VBM protocol, SPM2). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and violates no exclusion criteria (no ROI-only analysis, not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that includes a substance-using group (smokers) and reports participant demographics and MRI parameters, it does not provide a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise GM volume (e.g., VBM) between-group contrast of substance users versus controls. Analyses focus on cortical thickness within a set of 15 predefined ROIs (Desikan–Killiany–Tourville atlas) rather than whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain GM volume comparisons or coordinate tables of voxelwise results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses) and does not meet inclusion criteria I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast) nor I4 (voxelwise results/coordinates). It does meet I5 (reporting of participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and processing software).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent participants and healthy controls using whole-brain lobar and subcortical segmentation and between-group contrasts at multiple time points. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, MRI acquisition at 1.5T, segmentation/preprocessing details), Results (cross-sectional comparisons vs. controls and longitudinal analyses), and Discussion. This study is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of alcohol-dependent users vs controls and reports regional morphometry, but it used an ROI analysis (insula and ACC ROIs) rather than reporting any whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain between-group GM contrasts. Therefore it fails the required whole-brain evidence criterion. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only analysis with no qualifying whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences), I5 (reports participant demographics, substance characteristics, MRI details, and preprocessing). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of crack-cocaine (stimulant) users vs controls that reports GM volume differences and provides participant/MRI details (meets I2 and I5). However, the analyses extract regional cortical volumes using predefined ROIs (prefrontal, parietal, temporal, occipital) rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or coordinate-based voxelwise results. Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain results (fails I3) and constitutes an ROI-only analysis, which meets exclusion criterion E5. Conclusion: EXCLUDED (E5).

This is an empirical structural MRI study of adolescents with heavy prenatal alcohol exposure vs non-exposed controls that reports ACC volume/area/thickness from Freesurfer parcellation (ROI analyses). Inclusion met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM structural measures between exposed and control groups) and I5 (participant age/sex and MRI details reported). However it does NOT meet I3 (no whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported); results focus on ACC ROIs only. Therefore E5 applies (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM study comparing chronic cannabis users (n=11) to matched controls and reporting gray-matter volume and concentration analyses. The paper reports whole-brain between-group comparisons (noting no significant whole-brain differences) and voxelwise hippocampal results (modulated and unmodulated VBM), with coordinates and statistics. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (duration, THC/CBD hair measures), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. It is not ROI-only (whole-brain analyses were performed), and it is an original empirical study. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Note: sample size is small and some volume findings did not survive FWE correction, but these issues do not violate inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study that reports whole-brain vertexwise analyses (cortical thickness and volumetric measures) comparing children prenatally exposed to cannabis/tobacco vs nonexposed controls. It satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (reports whole-brain between-group GM contrast using vertexwise analyses), I4 (voxelwise/vertexwise results reported in the main text with clusterwise statistics), and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). However, it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I2 because the comparison is between offspring with prenatal exposure and controls, not between substance-using participants and controls; the meta-analysis objective specifically targets studies of substance users (current/former users) vs controls. No exclusion criteria (e.g., E5 ROI-only or E6 non-empirical) are met. The full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of nicotine users, but it assesses cortical thickness (surface-based measure) and reports region-specific (insula subregions) ROI analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise GM volume/density/concentration contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only ROI/subregional analyses with no qualifying whole-brain GM volume results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (study reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (does not assess GM volume/density/concentration as defined), I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast reported), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain coordinates/figures for GM volume). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on whole-brain GM volume/density voxelwise results.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of alcohol users but it does not include a control group nor report any whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. The analyses are correlational within a single sample and rely on ROI-based VBM/SBM measures of the right insula. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis requirement for between-group whole-brain GM comparisons. Exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses / no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criterion I5 (reporting of participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and software) is met. Inclusion criteria I2 (between-group GM differences vs controls), I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast), and I4 (whole-brain voxelwise results/coordinates) are not met. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I2: it reports cortical thickness (surface-based cortical thickness analysis) rather than grey matter volume/density/concentration measures required by I2. It does satisfy other inclusion criteria: whole-brain vertex-wise between-group contrasts with reported cluster coordinates (I3, I4) and reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical approach (I5). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are met. Full text appears complete. If the review were to accept cortical thickness as an eligible grey matter structural metric, this study would be potentially includable, but under the specified I2 (GM volume/density/concentration) it must be excluded.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of methamphetamine-dependent individuals vs. controls (stimulant class) using VBM methods, but the full text reports ROI-based VBM analyses (average modulated GM volumes extracted from 70 ROIs) and correlations rather than presenting whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate tables/figures. Inclusion I2 (empirical MRI GM comparison) and I5 (reporting participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software) are met. Inclusion I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast reported) is not met, and I4 (voxelwise results/coordinates available) is not met. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcoholics and controls that reports regional volumetric (segmentation) analyses (satisfies I2) and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and software used (FreeSurfer/CMA) (satisfies I5). However, the study does not present any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate-based VBM results; analyses are region-based volumetric/ROI comparisons only. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain evidence) and does not provide voxelwise results (I4 not met). As a result it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study with no qualifying whole-brain results) and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human MRI study that includes a whole-brain voxelwise VBM analysis comparing grey matter (GM) density between groups of smokers, ex-smokers, and non-smokers (nicotine user group vs controls). The methods describe whole-brain VBM processing and TFCE-corrected group comparisons, and the Results explicitly report VBM findings (no statistically significant GM differences). Participant demographics, substance-use history (pack-years, smoking duration), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FEAT, randomize) are reported. Although the VBM reported null results, the study meets inclusion criteria for whole-brain structural GM comparisons in nicotine users. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analysis or non-empirical paper) apply.

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study comparing alcohol use disorder (AUD) patients and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (GM density) and reporting whole-brain, voxelwise analyses. The Methods describe VBM preprocessing (SPM12/CAT12), MRI field strength (3T), and participant demographics/substance use details; results present whole-brain component maps differentiating AUD vs. controls (ICs) and their anatomical localization. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM differences), I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results presented in figures and localization reported), and I5 (reporting of age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing non-treatment-seeking cocaine-dependent individuals (stimulant users) to non-drug-using controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts with family-wise error-corrected results and xyz coordinates (left middle frontal gyrus) and provides coordinate-based correlations; results are presented in text, figures, and coordinates. Participant demographics (male, age range 20–55), substance use characteristics (cocaine use duration/frequency, comorbid substance use), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing male polysubstance users (n=46) to healthy controls (n=30). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts with FWE-corrected clusters and provides detailed voxel/cluster results and correlations. Participant age and sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical structural MRI study (English) comparing alcohol-dependent subjects and controls and reports regional volumetric differences using automated subcortical and hippocampal subfield segmentation (meets I2 and I5). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts or coordinate-based whole-brain results. Analyses are ROI/subfield based (Freesurfer segmentation and ANCOVA of regional volumes), so it does not provide the required whole-brain between-group GM comparisons. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses without qualifying whole-brain results).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing prescription opioid users to controls and reports participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details (meets I2 and I5). However, the VBM results presented derive from a priori/functional ROIs (L.NAc and L.vmPFC) extracted from rsFC findings rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast or coordinate tables/figures. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I3) and effectively reports ROI-only analyses, triggering exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete.

This longitudinal MRI study reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness comparisons between adolescents who initiated alcohol use and non-users, identifying a significant cluster (right middle frontal gyrus) with Talairach coordinates and cluster statistics, and also provides whole-brain analyses of other structural measures. Participant ages/sex, substance use characteristics, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, FSL, SPM) are reported. Although the study uses cortical thickness (surface-based) rather than VBM gray-matter volume per se, it addresses structurally altered grey matter with whole-brain between-group contrasts and supplies coordinate results, satisfying the review objective to identify consistent regions of altered GM between substance users and controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing cannabis users vs non-users. The paper reports whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts (SPM8) with region-level results (including family-wise error correction) and follow-up voxelwise/ROI analyses. Participant characteristics (mean age, familial risk, sex used as covariate), substance use measures (lifetime cannabis, alcohol, cigarettes), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL, SPSS) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete and reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses and a gene × smoking interaction on gray matter volume (left medial OFC) with coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English MRI study assessing GM differences between substance users and controls), I4 (voxelwise whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures), I5 (reports participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). However, the paper does not present a direct whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users (smokers) vs controls (nonsmokers) comparing GM volume (no main effect smoker vs control VBM contrast reported); therefore I3 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires an explicit whole-brain users-vs-controls GM contrast (I3), this study must be excluded.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume/density between smokers and never-smokers. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (SPM2; FDR-corrected results) with results presented in tables/figures and describes participant demographics (age/sex), smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study (3T) comparing alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls that reports gray-matter volume and cortical thickness differences using whole-brain surface-based analyses (vertex-wise processing and whole-brain/lobar/subcortical volume measures) processed with FreeSurfer. Participant demographics, abstinence duration, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software are reported. Results include whole-brain contrasts (total gray matter, whole-brain cortical thickness) and regional findings rather than ROI-only analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a longitudinal imaging study of first-episode schizophrenia patients treated with antipsychotics; it is not a study of substance users versus controls. It does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing substance users to non-using controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (study reports participant age/sex, some substance-use screening details, MRI field strength, preprocessing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users vs controls), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain results related to substance use). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (analyses are ROI-based/no qualifying whole-brain results relevant to substance-use contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for not addressing the review population/outcomes.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volumes between nicotine-dependent smokers and matched non-smoker controls. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (ANCOVA and post-hoc tests) with multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim) and presents results in figures/tables, with correlational analyses of pack-years and FTND. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8 with DARTEL; DPABI) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion sections. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis focused on GM differences in substance users (nicotine) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter between smokers (nicotine users: current/past) and nonsmokers. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (VBM, SPM2) with regions surviving FWE correction, and provides participant age/sex, smoking definitions, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software details. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing chronic cigarette smokers (n=44) and matched non-smoker controls (n=44). The paper reports whole‑brain, voxel-wise two-sample t-test contrasts in SPM5/VBM5.1 with cluster-level reporting (thresholds and cluster sizes described) and identifies regions of reduced gray matter in smokers. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (cigarettes/day, years smoking), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The study is not ROI-only and includes complete core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing older smokers (nicotine users) to matched never-smoker controls (N=39 pairs). The paper reports whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts (SPM2) with cluster results and coordinates described, and authors reran thresholds to confirm robustness. Participant demographics, smoking history, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, MATLAB, Stata) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No ROI-only or non-empirical study issues were identified. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing active methamphetamine (stimulant) users (n=17) to matched controls using voxel-based morphometry (whole-brain VBM) and ROI subcortical volumetry. The paper reports whole-brain between-group voxel-wise contrasts (GMD decreases and increases) and ROI volumetric results, and provides participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients vs controls that reports subcortical and global gray/white matter volume differences using automated segmentation (FSL FIRST) and vertex analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM/subcortical volume differences) and I5 (reports participant age, sex (all male), substance-use measures, MRI field strength 3T, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL)). However, the paper does not present a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast or VBM-style whole-brain analysis; analyses are based on segmented subcortical ROIs and surface vertex analyses. Thus it fails I3 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED per E5.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of nicotine (smoking) vs controls and reports regional volumetric results using FreeSurfer segmentation (meets I2 and I5). However, the paper reports ROI-based segmentation/volume analyses (subcortical nuclei, lobar WM, corpus callosum) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrast. No qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain mass-univariate GM results are reported, so it meets Exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore it fails Inclusion I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast) and I4 (qualifying voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion justified by E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing chronic smokers (n=22) to matched controls using voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) and reporting whole-brain between-group contrasts. The paper reports significant reductions in gray matter density in dlPFC and insula/operculum in smokers (with statistics), describes participant age/sex and smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Thus it satisfies the review’s criteria for inclusion and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing older smokers (substance users: nicotine) and never-smoker controls with voxelwise whole-brain analyses (tensor-based morphometry) reported using SPM5. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (UQ vs NS, SQ vs NS) with cluster-level results described in text/figures and Supplementary Table S2 (coordinates/regions). MRI scanner/model and acquisition parameters, participant ages and smoking history, and processing/statistical software are reported. It is not an ROI-only study and is not a review/meta-analysis. Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM differences between substance users and controls for nicotine.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter density between abstinent heroin-dependent individuals and matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group comparisons (two-sample t-tests, corrected) and identifies specific regions with reduced gray matter (right DLPFC, left IPL, etc.). Participant demographics, substance-use history (duration, abstinence), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM parameters) are reported. Results linking structural deficits to duration of heroin use are provided. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analysis or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter between opioid user groups and healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with coordinates (MNI) and supplementary tables, and uses appropriate preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) and a 3T scanner. Participant characteristics (age, sex—all male, substance use history, MRI field strength) are provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I2, I3, I4, I5). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not assess grey matter (GM) volume/density/concentration as required (I2 not met) and does not report any whole-brain between-group contrasts of GM volume (I3 not met). Instead, the paper reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical surface morphology measures (cortical thickness, surface area, gyrification), which do not satisfy the review's GM volume requirement. It does meet I5 (reports participant characteristics, MRI field strengths, and preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., it is not ROI-only nor non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing emerging adult marijuana users (n=15) to matched non-users (n=15). It reports whole-brain surface-based cortical thickness analyses (a whole-brain between-group contrast yielding a cluster-corrected difference in right fusiform gyrus) and subcortical volumetric analyses (thalamus, hippocampus, amygdala) with volumes analyzed relative to ICV. Methods and sample characteristics are reported (age/sex, substance use criteria, 3T MRI, FreeSurfer preprocessing). Although the study emphasizes cortical thickness rather than voxel-based GM volume/density, cortical thickness is a whole-brain grey-matter morphometric measure relevant to GM structural differences; subcortical GM volumes were also reported. Therefore the study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry that compares grey matter between substance users (separate cocaine and heroin groups) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (controls vs cocaine; controls vs heroin; direct cocaine vs heroin) with cluster-corrected statistics and anatomical coordinates (MNI→Talairach), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Key methodological details are provided (participant ages, years of abuse, 3T MRI acquisition, SPM5 preprocessing/statistics). The sample includes drugs of interest for the review (stimulant: cocaine; opioid: heroin), making the findings relevant to the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent participants (n=130) with healthy controls (n=69) using whole-brain vertex-wise (node-to-node) cortical thickness analyses. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (alcoholics vs. controls and sex-specific contrasts), regional results with coordinates/effect sizes, and relevant participant and MRI details (age/sex, substance use characteristics, 1.5T field strength, FreeSurfer processing, AFNI/SUMA statistics). Although the metric is cortical thickness rather than voxel-based GM volume/density, cortical thickness is a valid whole-brain structural grey-matter measure relevant to the review objective of identifying structural GM alterations in substance users. The study is not ROI-only and is empirical with original human MRI data, so it meets the inclusion requirements for whole-brain GM structural comparisons.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing adolescent heavy cannabis users and non-users using cortical thickness measures. The study performed whole-brain, vertex-wise group comparisons (clusterwise analysis) using FreeSurfer on 3T data and reports significant between-group cortical thickness differences (prefrontal, insula, and other regions) with ROI verification and correlations to substance-use variables. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for empirical MRI assessment of GM structural differences (cortical thickness as a grey-matter structural metric), includes whole-brain between-group contrasts, indicates availability of voxelwise/cluster results, and reports participant and acquisition/preprocessing details. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing DWI (alcohol-impaired driving) offenders and controls using whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness analyses and reporting coordinate clusters. It meets I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast) and I4 (voxelwise/vertex-wise results reported with coordinates/figures) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). However, it does NOT meet I2 because the primary morphometric measure is cortical thickness rather than grey matter volume/density/concentration (e.g., VBM measures) required by the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to failure to meet I2.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of cannabis users vs controls and reports lobar and global gray matter volumetry and detailed surface/gyrification measures. However, it does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts of gray matter volume or provide stereotactic coordinates (tables/figures/supplementary) required for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Therefore it cannot contribute qualifying whole-brain GM volume coordinates. Exclusion ID met: E5 (only region-level/lobar and surface analyses with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise GM results). Inclusion IDs met: I2 (empirical English MRI study assessing GM differences), I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and analysis software). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast reported), I4 (no voxelwise results/coordinates available). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of nicotine users (young adult smokers) vs matched controls that reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness analyses (surface-based whole-brain contrasts) and subcortical volume comparisons. It reports group-level significant cortical thickness reductions (vertex-wise, FDR-corrected) and subcortical volume differences, and provides participant demographics, smoking measures (pack-years, FTND), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, SPSS). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical structural MRI study with FreeSurfer-derived ROI volumes relating continuous substance-use measures across adolescence to regional volumes at age 25. However, it does not report any whole-brain between-group (substance users vs controls) voxelwise contrasts; analyses focus on specific ROIs and path models rather than case-control whole-brain comparisons. Therefore it meets exclusion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I5 (reporting participant demographics, substance use, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software) is satisfied. Inclusion criteria I2 (explicit between-group GM volume comparisons between substance users and controls) and I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast) are not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls, but it does NOT assess grey matter (GM) volume/density/concentration contrasts required by the review. Instead, it reports cortical thickness measures (68 Desikan-Killiany regions and vertex-based analyses restricted to selected regions) and examines correlations with neuroticism and interactions with AUD status. It does not present a whole-brain between-group voxelwise GM volume contrast of substance users vs controls. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I2 (GM volume differences) and I3 (whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast). The manuscript reports participant demographics and MRI preprocessing (satisfying I5). The analysis is effectively ROI/region-limited (and vertex analyses were restricted to implicated regions), so it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only/no qualifying whole-brain GM results). Inclusion criteria met: I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I2, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing older adult cannabis users (n=28) and nonusers (n=28) on gray matter volumes. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (VBM and surface-based GLMs) with multiple-comparison correction and cluster results (left lingual and rostral middle frontal cortex, putamen), includes participant demographics and substance-use details, and specifies MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FreeSurfer). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

Full text is complete. This study is an empirical MRI DBM study comparing alcoholic women and controls and reports whole-brain Jacobian maps (figures) and regional tests. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (voxelwise/figure-based whole-brain results are presented) and I5 (participant demographics, substance-use details, MRI parameters and preprocessing are reported). However it does NOT meet required inclusion criteria I2 and I3: the paper does not report whole-brain between-group contrasts specifically assessing grey matter (GM) volume differences (results focus on ventricles, white matter, and CSF; region-based tests target lateral ventricles, cortical white matter, corpus callosum, and CSF). No exclusion criteria (E5/E6) apply. Therefore exclude because it fails to provide GM-specific whole-brain between-group contrasts needed for the meta-analysis (I2 and I3 not met).

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (FreeSurfer-derived ROI and total GM) volumetric analyses and does not present a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast of substance users vs controls. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users/early-risk group and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength [3.0T], and preprocessing/statistical software [FreeSurfer]). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume reported); I4 (not applicable — no voxelwise whole-brain results available in main text/tables/figures). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent subjects (n=20) to matched controls (n=20), reporting whole-brain cortical volume and vertex-wise cortical thickness analyses with identified clusters of group differences. The paper provides participant demographics, substance-use measures, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (semiautomated Cardviews and FreeSurfer). Findings include total cortical volume reduction and multiple regional cortical thickness differences (clusters and system-level effects), with correlations to years of cocaine use. As a study of a stimulant (cocaine), it fits the review drug classes. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the study reports cortical thickness measured with FreeSurfer using a 34-region parcellation and repeated-measures regional analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise gray-matter volume/density contrasts with stereotactic coordinates. Participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T), smoking measures (cigarettes/day, pack-years), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer) are reported.
